forum.title: How to Use STL(Self Test Library)
forum.best_answer_content:
**Hello bupark007,**

Thank you for your reply.

When the first CRC calculated by the STL (the value in `R0`) is incorrect, this is typically due to a mismatch in the library configuration.

To ensure that everything is set up correctly for your device, could you please confirm whether the configuration macros in the `stl_user_param_template.c` file have been properly set?

You should have something similar to the following in this file:

```

#define STL_ROM_NO_TZ_START_ADDR (0x08000000UL) /* customizable */ /* No TZ */

#if defined (STM32H563xx)

#define STL_ROM_TZ_S_START_ADDR  (0x0C000000UL) /* customizable */ /* TZ, Secure Flash */

#define STL_ROM_TZ_NS_START_ADDR (0x08100000UL) /* customizable */ /* TZ, Non-Secure Flash */

#define STL_ROM_NO_TZ_END_ADDR   (0x081FFFFFUL) /* customizable */ /* no TZ: 2 Mbytes */

#define STL_ROM_TZ_S_END_ADDR    (0x0C0FFFFFUL) /* customizable */ /* TZ, Secure: 1 Mbytes */

#define STL_ROM_TZ_NS_END_ADDR   (0x081FFFFFUL) /* customizable */ /* TZ, Non-Secure: 1 Mbytes */

/* For all devices not supporting TrustZone, addresses related to TrustZone should be initialized to NULL value */

#elif defined (STM32H503xx)

#define STL_ROM_NO_TZ_END_ADDR   (0x0801FFFFUL) /* customizable */ /* no TZ: 128 Kbytes */

#define STL_ROM_TZ_S_END_ADDR     NULL

#define STL_ROM_TZ_NS_END_ADDR    NULL

#define STL_ROM_TZ_S_START_ADDR   NULL

#define STL_ROM_TZ_NS_START_ADDR  NULL

#else

#define STL_ROM_NO_TZ_END_ADDR   (0x0807FFFFUL) /* correct value for STM32H523VET6 */

#define STL_ROM_TZ_S_END_ADDR     NULL

#define STL_ROM_TZ_NS_END_ADDR    NULL

#define STL_ROM_TZ_S_START_ADDR   NULL

#define STL_ROM_TZ_NS_START_ADDR  NULL

#endif

```

Compared to the example, I added:

```

#define STL_ROM_NO_TZ_END_ADDR   (0x0807FFFFUL) /* correct value for STM32H523VET6 */

```

Then, for GCC, you should adapt the linker file as shown in the example below: (as in STM32H563ZITX\_FLASH.ld)

```

.data :

{

. = ALIGN(4);

_sdata = .;        /* create a global symbol at data start */

*(.data)           /* .data sections */

*(.data*)          /* .data* sections */

*(.RamFunc)        /* .RamFunc sections */

*(.RamFunc*)       /* .RamFunc* sections */

. = ALIGN(4);

_edata = .;        /* define a global symbol at data end */

_edata_load = LOADADDR(.data) + SIZEOF(.data) - 4; /* address of the last word of this section, which is also the last word in Flash */

} >RAM AT> FLASH

```

As described above, `_edata_load` defines the address of the last word in that section. You should add a similar definition to the last Flash section in your linker file in order to get the last address of your ROM code.

Of course, this piece of code should remain in your file, most likely in `Stl_scheduler.c`:

```

/* For GCC (STM32CubeIDE): */

#if (defined (__GNUC__) && !defined (__CC_ARM)  && !defined (__ARMCC_VERSION) )

/* symbol _edata_load is defined in linker-script. Its address is the last word of the used part of flash memory. */

extern void *_edata_load;

#define TEST_ROM_END_ADDR ( (uint32_t)&_edata_load + 3)

#endif /* __GNUC__ */

```

Could you please verify whether these conditions are satisfied?

Thanks,

Best regards
forum.author: bupark007

scraped_replies.html:
Hello bupark007,

Yes, the library is compatible with the STM32H523VET6 MCU.
The STM32H523VET6 features 512 KB of Flash, and I can confirm that your post-build command used to generate the CRC is correctly configured.

Reviewing the code, the following macro is correct:

#define TEST_ROM_START_ADDR 0x08000000U

However, the value of:

#define TEST_ROM_END_ADDR 0x0801A3FFU

is not correct. It should be:

#define TEST_ROM_END_ADDR 0x0807FFFFU

This means that the integrity check will cover the entire Flash bank.
Depending on your compiler, make sure that line 38 is not being built in this case.

Please let us know if this answer resolves your issue. Otherwise, we will investigate further. 

Thanks,
Best regards

scraped_replies.html:
Hello bupark007,

Unfortunately, it is not easy to debug the library because it is delivered without symbols or source code, for policy reasons.

However, I can suggest the following steps to help identify the issue:

First, I would recommend checking that the device has been properly flashed with the CRC table calculated through STM32CubeProgrammer using the post-build command.

After flashing the device, you should find the CRC table at the address calculated with the following formula:

p_crc = (uint32_t *)(TEST_ROM_END_ADDR - (4UL * (TEST_ROM_END_ADDR + 1UL - TEST_ROM_START_ADDR) / FLASH_SECTION_SIZE) + 1UL)

where FLASH_SECTION_SIZE = 1024.

Since the MCU Flash size is 512 KB, using:

TEST_ROM_START_ADDR = 0x08000000
TEST_ROM_END_ADDR   = 0x0807FFFF

the value of p_crc would be:

0x0807F800

So, if you go to this address, you should find something similar to the screenshot below.
 

If the CRC table is present, we can then compare the CRC calculated by the STL with the CRC stored in Flash.

To do this, set a breakpoint in the VerifySection function, after the call to STL_UTIL_CRC_Calculate, you will find the following instruction:

CMP R6, R0

like:

 

Here, R6 represents the CRC calculated by STM32CubeProgrammer, while R0 represents the CRC calculated by the STL.

 

Please note that, in some cases, STM32CubeProgrammer may fail to correctly calculate the last CRC value when the image size is not a multiple of 1024 bytes. For this reason, in the example, TEST_ROM_END_ADDR is defined as follows:

#pragma section = "FIXED_ORDER_ROM"
#define TEST_ROM_END_ADDR ((uint32_t)TEST_ROM_START_ADDR + __section_size("FIXED_ORDER_ROM") - 1)
#endif /* __ICCARM__ */

This allows the CRC calculation to be limited to the actual size of the image.

We also recommend keeping the EMPTY_PADDING block in the linker file to ensure that the image size ends with a 4-byte alignment.

Could you please verify the steps mentioned above and let us also know which compiler you are using?

Thanks
Best Regards
scraped_replies.author: SimoneST

scraped_replies.html:
Hello, thank you for the quick reply.

I am using the "STM32CubeIDE" tool and the "arm-none-eabi-gcc" compiler.

I verified the CRC value at address 0x0807F800 as shown in the figure below.

 

Additionally, after calling STL_UTIL_CRC_Calculate in the verifySection function and setting the endpoint, I confirmed that the R6 and R0 values ​​are different.

How can I verify why the R0 value is different?

R6 comes out as 0x6d398948, matching the address value of 0x0807F800, while R0 comes out as 0x9ee8b7cd.

Also, I understand that the example source code section you mentioned below is automatically selected and applied depending on the compiler.

/* Toolchain-dependent definitions of TEST_ROM_END_ADDR to define the end of the program in flash */
/* For Keil MDK: */
#if defined (__CC_ARM) || (defined (__ARMCC_VERSION) && (__ARMCC_VERSION >= 6010050))
/* Load$$LR$$LR_IROM1$$Limit is linker-defined symbol following the last byte of the used part of flash memory. */
extern void *Load$$LR$$LR_IROM1$$Limit;
#define TEST_ROM_END_ADDR ( (uint32_t) &Load$$LR$$LR_IROM1$$Limit - 1)
#endif /* _CC_ARM */

/* For GCC (STM32CubeIDE): */
#if (defined (__GNUC__) && !defined (__CC_ARM)  && !defined (__ARMCC_VERSION) )
/* symbol _edata_load is defined in linker-script. Its address is the last word of the used part of flash memory. */
extern void *_edata_load;
#define TEST_ROM_END_ADDR ( (uint32_t)&_edata_load + 3)
#endif /* __GNUC__ */

/* For IAR EWARM: */
#if defined (__ICCARM__)
/* All flash content has been placed in FIXED_ORDER_ROM. Its size is added to flash base address to calculate the address of its end.
   In linker-script, block FIXED_ORDER_ROM has been defined to contain entire content of flash.
   It is placed at the ROM origin and its length is used to calculate the address of its last byte. */
#pragma section = "FIXED_ORDER_ROM"
#define TEST_ROM_END_ADDR ( (uint32_t) TEST_ROM_START_ADDR + __section_size("FIXED_ORDER_ROM") -1)
#endif /* __ICCARM__ */

I understand that FIXED_ORDER_ROM is applied when using the IAR compiler; how can I apply it in GCC?

Thanks
Best Regards

scraped_replies.html:
Hello SimoneST

Thank you for your reply. I have already checked and tested the points mentioned above.

I have found the cause and would like to share it with you.

It turned out to be an issue with the build and download methods, not the source code.

When I proceeded to download the file while debugging in STM32CubeIDE after building the source code, the CRC error was STL_FAILED.

In STM32CubeIDE, I only performed Ctrl+B (Build) to create the *.bin file.

Then, I proceeded to download the *.bin file using STM32CubeProgrammer.

I confirmed that it is working without any issues.

Note: I have also modified the Post-Build Steps.

Existing: echo "\"STM32_Programmer_CLI.exe\" -sl \"%CD%\${BuildArtifactFileName}\" 0x08000000 0x08080000 0x400" > call_prg.bat && cmd /c call_prg.bat && arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary --gap-fill 0xFF "${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.elf" "${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.bin"

Change:arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary --gap-fill 0xFF "${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.elf" "${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.bin" && echo "\"STM32_Programmer_CLI.exe\" -sl \"%CD%\\${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.bin\" 0x08000000 0x08080000 0x400" > call_prg.bat && cmd /c call_prg.bat

That is all. Thank you for your response.

However, I could not find a solution for the STL_FAILED issue that occurs when downloading during Debug in STM32CubeIDE.

scraped_replies.html:
Hello bupark007,

Thank you very much for your feedback. I am glad to hear that you have found the root cause and that the issue is now almost resolved.

Regarding the new command you are using:

arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary --gap-fill 0xFF "${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.elf" "${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.bin" && echo "\"STM32_Programmer_CLI.exe\" -sl \"%CD%\\${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.bin\" 0x08000000 0x08080000 0x400" > call_prg.bat && cmd /c call_prg.bat

I noticed that STM32CubeProgrammer is being called with the .bin file as input. Typically, during debug, STM32CubeIDE flashes the .elf file instead, so that symbols are available for debugging.

Therefore, to make it work during debug, you could try using the same command but replacing the .bin file with the .elf file:

arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary --gap-fill 0xFF "${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.elf" "${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.bin" && echo "\"STM32_Programmer_CLI.exe\" -sl \"%CD%\\${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.elf\" 0x08000000 0x08080000 0x400" > call_prg.bat && cmd /c call_prg.bat

In other words, using ${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.elf instead of ${BuildArtifactFileBaseName}.bin  when calling the STM32_Programmer_CLI.exe. 
We should make sure that the CRC table is added to the same file that we are currently running/debugging.

Could you please confirm whether this works on your side?

Thanks,
Best regards!
